newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers vote for food policy based on science.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers vote for food policy based on science.

text.p: A UK farming audience rejected a call by consumers to oppose the idea of government food safety policy based on pure science.

In a formal debate late Tuesday at the Oxford farming conference, a majority of farmers agreed with the proposition put by UK Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell that "this house believes that decisions on food safety should be taken only on the basis of good science."
Sheila MacKechnie, director of the Consumers' Association, countered, "Food policy is not about good science. It is about the precautionary principle when you are dealing with animal health."
Dorrell said science could not provide absolute answers. "No human activity is totally safe."

MacKechnie said consumers knew they could not expect absolute safety, and that a vote in support of the motion would allow goverments to duck responsibility in a crisis by hiding behind the scientists. "The buck must rest with ministers," she said.
"Consumers these days do not trust the system of regulation and we have got to replace it with something that's more sustainable."
She failed to convince an audience largely composed of farmers, with 277 voting in favour of the motion proposed by Dorrell and 155 supporting MacKechnie.
